entries.words: its body runs along the ground on its legs, as most animals with four or more legs do
entries.reason: A body whose torso lies along the ground's plane, front to back: four legs, ten legs, or none (a slug), with necks forward, a tail behind and wings on its back. Most animals and most imagined beasts stand this way. A torso of one to eight segments bends enough to read as a back, a waist and a chest without a bone per vertebra.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica creature body grammar; see the entry reason

entries.words: stands upright on two legs, as a person does
entries.reason: A body whose torso stands on its legs, head on top and arms out to its sides in the rest pose, as a person's does; one or two pairs of legs. A creature that is a person's shape and fits a person's body (2,400 mm or less) is drafted onto the humanoid plan instead, so it wears people's looks and holds things in their hands.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica creature body grammar; see the entry reason

entries.words: a long body that lies along the ground
entries.reason: A body that is mostly its spine, lying straight along the ground in its rest pose and moved by a travelling wave when it goes: six to twenty-four segments make the wave read as a body rather than a few rods. It may rise into an upright torso at the front (a naga) and may have a few short legs (a lindworm).

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica creature body grammar; see the entry reason

entries.words: hangs in the air with nothing touching the ground
entries.reason: A body that floats: a short vertical torso with its tentacles hanging below and nothing on the ground. It has no legs; it moves only through the air.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica creature body grammar; see the entry reason

entries.words: a neck between its body and each head
entries.reason: Zero to eight neck bones per head: none for a beetle's head, two for a dog's, five or more for a dragon's or a swan's, which bend in a curve the drawing can follow.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica creature body grammar; see the entry reason

entries.reason: One to five heads, side by side at the front of the body, each on its own neck: a three-headed dog, a five-headed serpent. Every body has a head, which is where the drawing turns it to look.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica creature body grammar; see the entry reason

entries.words: a jaw that opens, which can carry things
entries.reason: A head may have a jaw, a bone that opens when it talks or bites and that carries one thing in its mouth when the body holds things with its jaws.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica creature body grammar; see the entry reason

entries.reason: Zero to sixteen tail bones from the hips back: a stub of one or two, a dog's four, a dragon's or a lizard's eight to sixteen, enough for the sway to curve.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica creature body grammar; see the entry reason

entries.words: an upright torso rising from the front of a long or four-legged body
entries.reason: Two bones rising from the front of a horizontal or serpentine body, carrying its arms and heads above it: a centaur's torso on a horse's body, a naga's on a serpent's.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica creature body grammar; see the entry reason

entries.words: legs it stands and walks on
entries.reason: Legs come in left and right pairs, zero to six pairs (a biped's one, a horse's two, an insect's three, a ten-legged monster's five), each of two to four segments from the hip to the foot. The front pair's feet carry things when the body holds things with its front claws.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica creature body grammar; see the entry reason

entries.reason: Arms come in left and right pairs, zero to three pairs, each of two to four segments from the shoulder to the hand; the first pair's hands carry things when the body holds things with its hands.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica creature body grammar; see the entry reason

entries.reason: Wings come in left and right pairs, zero to two pairs, each of two to four bones from the shoulder to the tip, with a membrane or feathers between them that the look draws; the span is the extent's.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica creature body grammar; see the entry reason

entries.reason: Fins come in left and right pairs along the body, zero to four pairs of one or two bones each.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica creature body grammar; see the entry reason

entries.reason: Zero to twelve tentacles in a ring under the body, each of two to eight segments so it can curl; they need not pair.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica creature body grammar; see the entry reason

spec.needs: legs, four or more tentacles, or a long body, and its feet on the ground

entries.reason: Walking is built: a body with at least one pair of legs, at least four tentacles or a serpentine body walks the world's walking surfaces by the walking module. A floating body never walks.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica creature body grammar; see the entry reason

spec.needs: a pair of wings, or a floating body
spec.refusal: This world has no flying creatures yet.

entries.reason: Flight for beings is a movement module not yet built here (flight version 2, for things a mind decides for, at any scale); until it is, a creature asked to fly is refused in these words. A body with a pair of wings or a floating body will fly by it.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica creature body grammar; see the entry reason

spec.needs: fins, four or more tentacles, or a long body
spec.refusal: This world has no swimming yet.

entries.reason: No world here has water a body moves through, and no swimming module is built; a creature asked to swim is refused in these words.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica creature body grammar; see the entry reason

spec.needs: legs, arms or four or more tentacles
spec.refusal: This world has no climbing yet.

entries.reason: No climbing module is built: walls and trees are not surfaces any body moves on here; a creature asked to climb is refused in these words.

licence.content_source: Authored for the Exulanica creature body grammar; see the entry reason

spec.refusal: This world has no burrowing yet.

entries.reason: No world here has ground a body moves through, and no burrowing module is built; a creature asked to burrow is refused in these words.

entries.words: what every body here is held to
entries.reason: At most 128 bones (the most joints the browser skins in one look), an appearance of 12 to 200 characters for the sculptor (enough for a sentence, short enough to carry no story), and two to four colours for the sketch: a body, a belly, an accent and its eyes.
